Distinguish statements, blocks and comments
Apply standard Java naming conventions

exercises.title: Write your own greeting
exercises.prompt: Create `Intro.java` with a public class `Intro` whose `main` method prints two lines: your name, and the language you want to learn next. Compile and run it from a terminal.
hints: The file name must match the public class name exactly, including capital letters.
Use two `System.out.println` statements, one per line.
checks: The file is named Intro.java and the class is Intro
java Intro prints two lines: your name, then a language

exercises.title: Break it on purpose
exercises.prompt: Delete one semicolon from `Intro.java` and compile. Read the error and find the line it reports. Restore the semicolon, then rename the class to `intro` (lowercase) without renaming the file, and compile again. Compare the two errors.
hints: Compiler errors name the file, a line number and a short description.
The second error says a public class must be declared in a file with a matching name.
checks: I saw a compile error after deleting the semicolon and found its line number
I saw a different error after renaming the class to lowercase
I restored the program and it compiles again

exercises.title: Fix the broken program
exercises.prompt: This program has two syntax errors. Find and fix both by reading, then compile to check yourself.
hints: One statement is missing its terminator.
Count the opening and closing braces.
checks: I found the missing semicolon without compiling
I found the missing closing brace

title: Lifecycle of a Program
description: How source becomes a running program: javac produces bytecode, the JVM loads, verifies and executes it; how JDK, JRE and JVM relate; setting up a JDK and IDE.
objectives: Explain compile-time versus run-time steps
Differentiate JDK, JRE and JVM
Install a JDK and compile and run a program from the command line and an IDE

subtopics.summary: What javac produces and why .class files exist.

subtopics.summary: The java launcher, class names and source-file mode.

subtopics.summary: Setting up and checking your tools.

exercises.title: Compile and run from a terminal
exercises.prompt: Save the `Greeter` program from the Code tab as `Greeter.java`. In that folder run `javac Greeter.java`, list the folder, then run `java Greeter`. Write down which new file appeared and which command created it.
hints: If `javac` is not found, you installed a runtime without the compiler. Install a JDK.
Use the class name, not the file name, with `java`.
checks: javac created Greeter.class next to Greeter.java
I can say which command made the .class file

exercises.title: One compile-time error, one run-time error
exercises.prompt: Create a program that fails to compile (for example, misspell `System`) and one that compiles but fails when run (for example, the `Divide` program). For each, note which command printed the error and what the message looked like.
hints: Compile-time errors appear when you run `javac`, before any program output.
Run-time errors appear after compilation succeeds, when you run `java`.
checks: The misspelled System failed at javac, before anything ran
Divide compiled but failed when run with java
I can explain why the compiler could not see the second error

exercises.title: Try source-file mode
exercises.prompt: Delete `Greeter.class`, then run `java Greeter.java`. Check the folder afterward. Is there a new `Greeter.class`? What does that tell you about where the compiled code went?
hints: It suits one-file programs but produces no class files to distribute.
checks: I can explain where the compiled code went

title: Data Types
description: Primitive and reference types, their sizes and ranges, default values and literals.
objectives: List the eight primitive types and their ranges
Contrast primitives with reference types
Choose an appropriate type for a value

title: Variables and Scopes
description: Declaring, initializing and naming variables, and where each one is visible and for how long.
objectives: Declare and initialize local variables, including var
Predict visibility across block, method and class scope
Explain variable shadowing

title: Type Casting
description: Widening and narrowing conversions, implicit promotion in expressions, and casting between reference types.
objectives: Predict implicit widening in expressions
Perform narrowing casts and anticipate data loss
Use instanceof before a reference cast

title: Math Operations
description: Arithmetic, compound, relational and logical operators, precedence, integer versus floating-point division, overflow and the Math class.
objectives: Evaluate expressions using operator precedence
Avoid integer-division and overflow surprises
Use Math methods for rounding, powers and roots

title: Conditionals
description: Branching with if/else, the ternary operator, switch statements and switch expressions.
objectives: Write if/else chains and nested conditions
Choose between switch statements and switch expressions
Use boolean logic and short-circuiting correctly

title: Loops
description: Repetition with for, enhanced for, while and do-while, plus break, continue and labeled loops.
objectives: Choose the right loop for a task
Control iteration with break and continue
Avoid off-by-one and infinite-loop errors

title: Strings and Methods
description: Working with String, immutability, comparison and StringBuilder; defining methods with parameters and return values.
objectives: Use common String methods for searching and slicing
Explain string immutability and when to use StringBuilder
Define and call methods with parameters and return values

title: Arrays

objectives: Declare, initialize and traverse arrays
Work with two-dimensional arrays
Use Arrays.sort, copyOf and toString

title: Basics of OOP

objectives: Describe objects, classes and messages between objects
Name the four pillars of OOP
Sketch a real-world thing as a class

title: Classes and Objects
description: Declaring a class, creating instances with new, and the difference between a class, an object and a reference.
objectives: Declare a class with fields and a constructor
Create and use several instances
Explain reference variables versus objects

title: Attributes and Methods
description: Instance fields, instance methods and this: how behavior reads and changes an object's state.
objectives: Add fields and methods to a class
Use this to disambiguate names
Distinguish fields from local variables

title: Static Keyword
description: Static fields, methods and blocks: members that belong to the class rather than to an instance.
objectives: Declare class-level fields and methods
Explain why static methods cannot use this
Recognize good and bad uses of static

title: Method Chaining
description: Returning this or a new object from methods so calls read fluently, as in builders and StringBuilder.
objectives: Design methods that return this for fluent calls
Compare mutable chaining with immutable return-new-object style
Implement a simple builder

title: Object Lifecycle
description: From allocation and constructors through use to unreachability and garbage collection.
objectives: Write overloaded constructors and chain them with this(...)
Trace initialization order
Explain when an object becomes eligible for garbage collection

title: Initializer Block

objectives: Write instance and static initializer blocks
Predict initialization order
Decide when a block beats a constructor

title: Final Keyword
description: final variables, parameters, methods and classes: constants, blocking overriding and blocking inheritance.
objectives: Declare constants and blank finals
Explain final references versus immutable objects
Apply final to methods and classes deliberately

title: Pass by Value / Pass by Reference
sourceLabel: Pass by Value / Pass by Reference
description: How arguments are passed: Java always copies values, and for objects the copied value is a reference.
objectives: Predict the effect of modifying parameters inside a method
Explain why reassigning a parameter does not affect the caller
Show how mutating a passed object is visible to the caller

title: Access Specifiers
description: public, protected, package-private and private: what each exposes and to whom.
objectives: State the visibility of each access level
Choose the narrowest access that works
Explain protected across packages

title: Encapsulation
description: Hiding state behind a class's interface with private fields, accessors and invariants.
objectives: Protect fields with private access and accessors
Enforce invariants in setters and constructors
Explain why exposing internals harms maintainability

title: Packages
description: Organizing classes into packages: naming, imports, directory layout and the default package.
objectives: Place classes in packages and import them
Match package names to directory layout
Resolve name clashes between imported classes

title: Nested Classes
description: Static nested, inner, local and anonymous classes, and when each is appropriate.
objectives: Distinguish the four kinds of nested class
Access enclosing state from an inner class
Replace an anonymous class where appropriate

title: Inheritance
description: Extending classes with extends and super, constructor chaining, the IS-A relationship and the Object class.
objectives: Create a subclass that reuses and extends a superclass
Call superclass constructors and methods
Choose between inheritance and composition

title: Method Overloading / Overriding
description: Overloading (same name, different parameters, chosen at compile time) versus overriding (subclass redefinition, chosen at run time), with @Override.
objectives: Write overloaded methods and predict which is chosen
Override methods correctly with @Override
State the rules for overriding signatures and access

title: Static vs Dynamic Binding
description: Which implementation runs: compile-time binding for static, private and final members and for fields; run-time dispatch for overridden instance methods.
objectives: Predict output when reference and object types differ
Explain why fields and static methods are not polymorphic
Describe virtual dispatch at a high level

title: Abstraction
description: Abstract classes and methods: sharing structure while leaving specifics to subclasses.
objectives: Declare abstract classes and methods
Implement an abstract method in a subclass
Decide between abstract class and interface

title: Interfaces
description: Contracts without instance state: abstract, default, static and private methods, multiple implementation and interface-based design.
objectives: Define and implement interfaces
Use default and static interface methods
Program to an interface rather than a class

title: Enums
description: Fixed sets of named constants with fields, constructors and methods; EnumMap and EnumSet; use in switch.
objectives: Declare an enum with fields and methods
Use enums in switch expressions
Choose EnumMap or EnumSet appropriately

title: Record
description: Concise immutable data carriers: canonical and compact constructors, generated accessors, equals, hashCode and toString.
objectives: Declare records and use generated members
Validate in a compact constructor
Choose between record, class and enum

title: Regular Expressions
description: Pattern and Matcher: matching, capturing groups, replacing and splitting text with regex syntax.
objectives: Write patterns using classes, quantifiers and groups
Extract captured groups with Matcher
Avoid catastrophic backtracking

title: Array vs ArrayList
description: Trade-offs between fixed arrays and growable ArrayList, the List interface, and where LinkedList fits.
objectives: Compare arrays and ArrayList for size, speed and API
Use List operations: add, get, remove, sort
Choose ArrayList or LinkedList for a workload

title: Queue

objectives: Use offer, poll and peek correctly
Explain FIFO versus priority ordering
Pick an implementation for a use case

title: Dequeue

title: Stack

objectives: Apply push, pop and peek
Solve a balanced-brackets problem with a stack
Explain why the Stack class is discouraged

title: Set

title: Map

Iterate keys, values and entries

title: Iterator

objectives: Traverse with Iterator and enhanced for

Make a custom class Iterable

title: Exception Handling
description: try/catch/finally, checked versus unchecked exceptions, throws, try-with-resources and custom exceptions.
objectives: Catch and handle specific exceptions
Distinguish checked from unchecked exceptions
Write try-with-resources and custom exceptions

title: I/O Operations
description: Byte and character streams, readers and writers, buffering, and the Console and Scanner.
objectives: Read and write data with streams and readers
Apply buffering and close resources safely
Choose between byte and character streams

title: File Operations
description: Files and paths with java.nio.file: reading, writing, copying, walking directories and file attributes.
objectives: Read and write files with Files and Path
List and walk directories
Handle missing files and permissions

title: Networking

Call an HTTP API with HttpClient
Explain request, response, status codes and headers

title: Generic Collections

title: Annotations

title: Modules
